title: WTA Finals 2026: Singles semifinals set after Elina Svitolina shocks Aryna Sabalenka
content:
As the WTA Finals prepares for its next chapter, this year’s is still being written.

After an early end to the deal to host its flagship event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, the WTA is stopping off at Indian Wells, Calif., before a three-year run in Charlotte, N.C. Over those four editions, the governing body intends to restore its flagship event’s status and relevance, starting this November in the Coachella Valley.

The eight best singles players and doubles pairs of the season compete. The tournament was set to be headlined by the new world No. 1, Elena Rybakina, and the player she dethroned, world No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka. But Rybakina, this year’s Australian Open and U.S. Open champion, withdrew due to a viral illness on the eve of the tournament. Sabalenka, who lost to Rybakina in both of those Grand Slam finals, will look to make a statement heading into 2027.

French Open champion Mirra Andreeva and Wimbledon champion and finalist, Linda Nosková and Karolína Muchová, made their debuts at the event. Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula of the U.S. return and Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina looks to cap her best season in a long time. She was ultimately joined by compatriot Marta Kostyuk, who replaces Rybakina as an alternate.

Here’s everything you need to know about the tournament, with the schedule and results updated day by day.

The singles semifinals will pit Jessica Pegula against Mirra Andreeva and Elina Svitolina against Linda Nosková.

Svitolina stunned Aryna Sabalenka to seal a place in the last four, while Pegula knocked out Coco Gauff by defeating Nosková. Pegula and Andreeva will meet for the first time, after a hot mic caught Pegula’s labeling Andreeva a “diva” before the start of the tournament. The duo has since laughed it off.

The eight players who qualified were split into four pots for the draw. Pot 1 is No. 1 and No. 2, Pot 2 is No. 3 and No. 4, and so on.

These seedings follow the players’ rankings in the WTA Race, a table that counts only ranking points earned in 2026.

Each player then plays three round-robin matches. The top two players from each group contest the semifinals, with the winners meeting in the final.

The tournament starts Nov. 8. There are six days of round-robin competition, with two singles matches and two doubles matches per day. The singles matches are played first, starting at 12 p.m. PT / 3 p.m. ET.

On Nov. 14, it is semifinal day, with singles again followed by doubles and play again starting at 12 p.m. PT. The finals follow the same schedule on Nov. 15.

There is coverage on Tennis Channel in the U.S. and Sky Sports in the U.K.

Rybakina won the singles title at the 2025 WTA Finals, held in Riyadh. She defeated Sabalenka 6-3, 7-6(0) in the final, winning all five of her matches at the event. The title earned Rybakina the largest winner’s check in women’s sports history, at $5,235,000.

In the doubles, Russia’s Veronika Kudermetova and Belgium’s Elise Mertens defeated Hungary’s Tímea Babos and Brazil’s Luisa Stefani in the final, 7-6(4), 6-1. They split just over $1 million.

This year’s prize pool is $10 million, with $8 million for the singles competition and $2 million. It is allocated per match win and structured so the singles champion takes home the biggest prize if they go through the event undefeated with five wins (three round-robin wins, a semifinal win, and then victory in the final).

Last year’s prize pool was $15.5 million.

The winner of the singles final will receive $3.37 million, while the winner of each semifinal will receive $820,000; the prize for a round-robin match win is $230,000 and each singles player receives $220,000 just for appearing at the event, provided that they play all three of their round-robin matches.

The winning doubles pair will receive $725,000 if they go undefeated.

Round-robin wins carry 200 points, a semifinal win carries 400 points and a final win carries 500 points. An undefeated champion (three round-robin wins, a semifinal win and a final win) will earn 1,500 points.

Saudi Arabia’s sports ministry and the Saudi Tennis Federation completed a three-year deal for the WTA Finals in April 2024. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund already sponsored the ATP and WTA world rankings, and this deal was the biggest element of the kingdom’s push into tennis before it announced an ATP Masters 1000 tournament that will start as early as 2028.

That deal ended a year early, in part because of the Iran conflict but also because the WTA Finals had outlived its usefulness to Saudi Arabia’s wider tennis ambitions, two people briefed on its sports ministry’s operations, speaking on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, said.

“We have an incredible opportunity to bring the WTA Finals, a world-class, premium global event showcasing the best in women’s tennis, to a new home,” a spokesperson for the WTA said in a statement following the announcement of the early departure from Saudi Arabia.

That departure left the WTA Tour in need of a venue for 2026, and it alighted on Indian Wells, where the prestigious ATP Masters 1000 and WTA 1000 event is held each March. From 2027, the WTA Finals will be held in Charlotte, N.C., for at least three years.
